_about: pe67 open-source material assemblage table for Proto-Elamite tablet sites, plus the Ur III province control table. Ordinal codes: 2 = production/workshop or dominant handled good attested; 1 = present/handled (finished objects, consumption); 0 = not reported in the sources consulted. Archaeological data only; no sign readings. Coding is coarse and partly from secondary summaries; cycle 3 of pe67 perturbs it. 'kind': GRAIN-like goods must be counted with a capacity (C) system; OBJ/ANIMAL with a counting system (SDB/B); EITHER may take any system.

PE_sources.Susa: Susa III / Acropole I 16-14B: bevelled-rim bowls, sealed jars, bitumen-compound objects, copper objects, imported stones (Le Brun 1971, 1978 CahDAFI; summary in CONTEXT.md and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susa). Coded as the hub's generic urban assemblage.
PE_sources.Malyan: Banesh TUV: copper production debris and metallurgy, marine shell working, lapis and carnelian ornaments, flint technology, raw materials and by-products (Nicholas 1990, The Proto-Elamite Settlement at TUV, Malyan Excavation Reports 1, https://www.penn.museum/research/publications/publication/959 ; https://repo.library.stonybrook.edu/xmlui/handle/11401/88660). Fauna: sheep/goat dominant, cattle present, provisioned cuts in administrative areas (Zeder 1991; https://opencontext.org/projects/d6b25ec9-2884-4e3c-00e8-0c5a6472fa63). Grain: barley and wheat (Miller, in Sumner 2003 Early Urban Life in the Land of Anshan).
PE_sources.Yahya: IVC building: bevelled-rim bowls, cylinder seals and sealings, 84 blank tablets, copper spearhead (IVC2); chlorite/steatite manufacture (>1,000 pieces) is attested in IVB, directly after IVC, so coded 2 with a period caveat (cycle 3 recodes to 1). Shell coded 1 (Gulf access). Potts 2001, Excavations at Tepe Yahya 1967-1975: The Early Periods (ASPR 45); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tepe_Yahya ; https://www.iranicaonline.org/?p=2043.
PE_sources.Sialk: Sialk III-IV: large-scale metallurgy (slag, crucibles, moulds) including silver cupellation with litharge cakes (furnace 14C 3660-3520 BCE); Arisman nearby (arsenical copper, speiss, silver). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tepe_Sialk ; https://publikationen.uni-tuebingen.de/xmlui/handle/10900/51674.
PE_sources.Sofalin: Tokens, bullae, sealings, blank tablets, bevelled-rim bowls (beeswax residue by GC-MS), furnaces for silver processing, child jar burials. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tepe_Sofalin ; Hessari & Akbari, https://jarcs.ut.ac.ir/article_81253_4cb6da643d1392ef1b399e80e2acf8ea.pdf.
PE_sources.Ozbaki: Ozbaki (Savojbolagh): one PE tablet; early metallurgy reported in summaries; coded minimally (copper 1, grain 1). Weakest row.
PE_sources.Shahr-i Sokhta: Period I-II: lapis lazuli (Badakhshan) and carnelian bead working with flint drills, Gulf shell, local copper, textile industry. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahr-e_Sukhteh ; https://iris.unito.it/handle/2318/2096024. Lapis workshops are best dated c. 2500 BCE (later than the PE tablet), a period caveat.

UR3_sources: Province specialisms from standard archive descriptions (Drehem livestock centre; Umma timber, reed and grain domains; Girsu grain, fisheries and textile mills; Garšana construction of an estate; Irisagrig messenger rations of beer, bread and oil; Nippur temple offerings; Ur textile and craft workshops). Used only as the known site-product truth of the control; the words are reduced to opaque ids.
